I'm a fan of KeePass. Know of any other good ones?

that's the best one, IMHO. I prefer the 1.x version over the 2.x version that has .net or mono requirements. But it's open source, in fact, it's getting a code audit soon.

http://www.ghacks.net/2016/07/22/keepass-password-manager-icode-audit/
Do you have a general rundown of the differences? I have heard that mono is a security risk for Linux machines, but I don't know why.

I don't know if mono is a security problem or not. I know Linux guys typically hate mono as it's seen as an invasion of Microsoft code into the unix ecosystem, and along with that there's potential problems for patent issues. Microsoft has a history of "embrace. extend. extinguish." when it comes to open protocols and open source in general, so a lot of open source advocates are wary of anything that runs MS code on a Linux system, sometimes unfairly.

The reason I prefer the 1.x version more than the 2.x version is that I simply like my applications to be Portable. If an application requires this massive run-time environment, then it's not portable. I dislike .Net apps for the same reason I hate Java apps or anything that requires a C++ runtime be installed.

I can run the Windows version of Keepass 1.x off a thumb drive on ANY windows computer: http://portableapps.com/apps/utilities/keepass_portable

You couldn't do this with the 2.x version b/c every computer would need to have .Net installed.

If I come across a Linux machine that say.. doesn't have keepass installed, that's fine. I can run that portable windows version with WINE.

In Linux, there's also the KeepassX project, which is better than KeepPass itself. KeepassX only supports one database version at a time. They used to support 1.x, now they only support 2.x. I basically run a slightly older 1.x version I built from source.

But as for differences? The stock applications aren't different at all. The 1.x and 2.x have the same functionality. The only difference is that there are a lot of plugins that work for 2.x that don't work for 1.x. I, personally, don't fuck with plugins on my password manager. It does everything i need out of the box.
